In the 1950s, a scientist named Homi Bhabha made a prediction that sounded insane: that the sand on India's beaches would one day power the entire country for centuries. He designed a 70-year plan to make it happen, and died before seeing a single step of it work. On April 6, 2026, India took the second step in that plan — becoming only the second country on Earth to achieve something the US, Japan, Germany, and France all attempted, spent billions on, and abandoned. The goal: to never buy fuel from anyone ever again.
